reading.body:
SAIC's patent record does not match its AI services pitch: its 21 granted patents are vehicle and battery hardware, not AI.

The five most recent grants cover battery insulation monitoring, drive motor cooling, battery modules and storage, and a flexible air conditioner vent. These are mechanical and electrical inventions for vehicles and cooling, filed and granted between December 2025 and September 2026. The company's own description, by contrast, is entirely about AI services for defense and civilian government, including two IDC MarketScape recognitions in 2025.

The mismatch matters because AI capability is usually traced to compute, and compute to power and cooling. SAIC's patents sit on the cooling and battery side of that chain, but for vehicles rather than data centers. Nothing in the data connects these inventions to AI workloads, and the patent set is a keyword match on the applicant phrase "saic," which may capture unrelated filings.

What the data does not show is how SAIC actually delivers AI, what infrastructure it runs on, or whether it owns or leases data center capacity. It records no products, no lawsuits, and no MCP servers. The patent count covers grants since 2001 only, so it says nothing about pending applications or about work done under government contracts, which is where a services firm's real technical output would sit.

profile_text.body:
SAIC is a publicly traded company, listed under the ticker SAIC, that describes itself as a provider of AI services. On its own site it says it was recognized as a worldwide leader in AI services in the IDC MarketScape: Worldwide AI Services for National Civilian Government 2025 Vendor Assessment, and as a leader in AI services in the IDC MarketScape: U.S. Defense and Intelligence Agencies AI Services 2025 Vendor Assessment.

The site presents applied AI as a way for defense leaders to achieve decision dominance by turning large volumes of data into fast, mission-ready insight. It also describes RAG-R as redefining national security and warfighting AI through secure deployment, real-time knowledge updates, and structured, trustworthy reasoning. No products, lawsuits, or MCP servers are recorded for the company.
